The process ends with the Quality Management team, marking the completion of the entire procedure.

The process begins when a backend technician submits an order. The technician then collects the required medicine and places it into a bag. After collecting the medicine, the technician moves the bag to the Quality Assurance (QA) area.

Next, a pharmacist verifies the contents of the bag to ensure everything is correct. After verification, the pharmacist checks if the order requires special attention. If it does, the pharmacist marks the bag with an 'X'. Regardless of whether the bag is marked, the pharmacist places it in the pickup area.

Once the bag is in the pickup area, the process waits for the customer to arrive. When the customer arrives, a customer service representative retrieves the order details using the customer's ID. The representative then collects the bag from the back area.

The representative checks if the bag has an 'X' mark. If there is no 'X', the bag is given to the pharmacist for further evaluation. The pharmacist decides if it is safe to give the bag to the customer. If it is safe, the pharmacist hands the bag to the customer, completing the order fulfillment. If it is not safe, the pharmacist removes any unsafe medicine and records the removal before giving the bag to the customer.

If the bag has an 'X' mark, the customer service representative directly hands the bag to the customer and marks it as delivered, ending the process.

The process begins with the Hamburg Fair initiating a new fair. The first task is to create a traffic guide, which is handled by Hamburg Fair. Once the traffic guide is created, it is published by Hamburg Fair.

Exhibitors then read the published traffic guide. After reading the guide, they encounter a decision point: whether online booking is required. If online booking is necessary, exhibitors proceed to create an account in the booking portal. Following this, they book a time slot. Once the time slot is booked, exhibitors proceed to book a forklift. The forklift booking data is received by Kühne and Nagel.

If online booking is not required, exhibitors directly proceed to the check-in process. At check-in, there is another decision point: whether a delivery slip is available. If a delivery slip is not available, Kühne and Nagel create the delivery slip. If a delivery slip is available, Kühne and Nagel validate the delivery information.

Once the delivery information is validated, the truck arrives at the buffer place, managed by the exhibitors. The truck then proceeds to the designated entrance gate. At the entrance gate, Hamburg Fair scans the delivery slip for entry. After entry, the truck parks at the unloading point. Hamburg Fair then scans the delivery for unloading, and the cargo is unloaded.

After unloading, Hamburg Fair scans the delivery slip for exit. The truck exits the fair, and Kühne and Nagel ensure that the unloading area is set free. This marks the end of the logistics process. Throughout the process, Kühne and Nagel send SMS notifications for fair entrance and delivery slips as needed. Additionally, logistics input is sent by Kühne and Nagel to the relevant parties.

The process begins when the submission of applications ends. The secretariat at the university starts by verifying the application documents. If the application is deemed unacceptable, the secretariat informs the candidate that the application is denied, and the process ends there.

If a document is missing, the secretariat asks the candidate to bring or mail the missing document. Once the document is received, the secretariat re-verifies the application documents.

If the application is acceptable, the secretariat checks the application further. If the application is denied at this stage, the secretariat informs the candidate of the denial, and the process ends.

If the application is accepted, the secretariat adds the candidate to the accepted candidate list. The secretariat then informs the candidate that the application was accepted. The candidate is required to pay an amount in advance. A one-week deadline is set for this payment.

After the deadline, the secretariat checks whether the candidate has paid. If the candidate did not pay, the secretariat chooses a runner-up and informs them that their application was accepted, continuing the process from the payment step.

If the candidate paid in advance, they bring an additional application, and the secretariat officially accepts the candidate to the university, ending the process.

If the candidate declines, they bring an application of decline, and the secretariat chooses a runner-up, informing them of their acceptance, and the process continues from the payment step.

The process begins when a symptomatic patient is referred to the Urology Unit. The Urology Unit then performs a digital rectal examination (DRE) and checks PSA levels. Following this, the Urology Unit counsels the patient on the results of these tests.

Next, the Urology Unit discusses the implications of both negative and positive biopsy results with the patient. After this discussion, informed consent is received from the patient. Once consent is obtained, the Urology Unit performs a prostate biopsy. This procedure is conducted by a trained urologist or radiologist using a transrectal ultrasound with biopsy needles placed either transrectally or transperineally.

The specimen from the biopsy is then analyzed by the Pathology Unit. After analysis, the Pathology Unit sends a report to the Urologist. The Urology Unit receives this report and proceeds to evaluate the results. If the results are negative, the Urology Unit repeats the PSA and DRE tests within 12 months. The results of these repeated tests are then evaluated again. If the results remain negative, the Urology Unit counsels the patient on risk factors and discharges them, noting that prostate cancer may still be present, especially if the biopsy showed ASAP or an abnormal DRE.

If the results are positive at any point, the Urology Unit schedules an appointment with the Radiology Unit. The Radiology Unit performs imaging, which may include an isotope bone scan, CT scan, prostate MRI, or interval imaging to determine the appropriate timing of androgen deprivation therapy (ADT). After performing the imaging, the Radiology Unit sends a report to the Urologist.

Upon receiving the report from the Radiologist, the Urology Unit conducts TNM staging and assigns a Gleason Grade Score. The clinical stage of the tumor is recorded in the medical records. Following this, the Urology Unit engages in treatment planning. Once the treatment plan is finalized, the treatment is initiated, marking the end of the process.

The process begins when a potential employee presents themselves to Human Resources. Human Resources advises the potential employee to undertake a pre-employment medical examination. The employee then undertakes the pre-employment medical.

After completing the medical, there is a decision point to determine if the employee has passed the medical examination. If the employee does not pass, the process ends with the employee declining employment. If the employee passes, Human Resources registers the employee for online induction by sending an email or link.

Following this, two tasks occur simultaneously. The employee undertakes the online site induction, and Human Resources inputs the employee's details into the SAP system, attaching the task profile. Once the online site induction is complete, that part of the process ends.

After the employee's details are entered into SAP, an Admin Support Officer inputs the employee's completed training and qualifications. This leads to two simultaneous tasks: Human Resources advises the employee to undertake an HR induction on their first day, and the Admin Support Officer creates a card for the employee.

The HR induction involves the employee undertaking the HR induction process. After this, Human Resources escorts the employee to the Crew Leader. The Crew Leader then determines the required training for the employee, and the employee undertakes department-specific induction training. Once this training is complete, the employee is considered fully inducted.

Meanwhile, after the card is created, the Admin Support Officer issues the card to the employee via the security gate. The process concludes with the card being delivered to the Crew Leader.

The process begins with customers initiating the procedure by filling out the required documents. Once completed, these documents are sent to the car rental system.

The car rental system receives the documents and proceeds to check if all necessary documents are present. At this point, the system evaluates whether additional documents are needed. If more documents are required, the system requests them from the customers. The customers then provide the additional documents, which are sent back to the car rental system for another check.

If all required documents are in order, the car rental system lists all available cars for the customers. The customers then select a car from the list and proceed to make a reservation.

Once the reservation is made, the information is sent to the car dealer. The car dealer checks the reservation details and provides feedback on the reservation status, completing the process.

The process begins when a customer's phone is damaged. The customer initiates the process by returning the damaged phone to the company, XYZ Phone SDN BHD.

Once the company receives the damaged phone, they proceed to check if the phone is still under warranty. This is a decision point where two outcomes are possible:

1. If the phone is not under warranty, XYZ Phone SDN BHD rejects the warranty claim. They then send a rejection notice along with the damaged phone back to the customer. The process ends here with the claim being rejected.

2. If the phone is under warranty, XYZ Phone SDN BHD registers the warranty claim. They then diagnose the problem with the damaged phone.

After diagnosing the problem, the company repairs the damaged phone. Once repaired, the phone undergoes testing to ensure the problem is fixed. This is another decision point:

- If the problem is not fixed, the phone is sent back for further repairs, and the testing process is repeated.

- If the problem is fixed, XYZ Phone SDN BHD sends the fixed phone back to the customer.

Upon receiving the fixed phone, the customer acknowledges the receipt, and the process concludes with the claim being approved.

The process begins with the deliveryman receiving live fish from the port. Once the fish are received, the deliveryman assists in loading the goods onto a vehicle. After loading, the deliveryman drives to the warehouse.

Upon arrival at the warehouse, the warehouse crew receives and offloads the fish from the delivery truck. The crew then partitions the fish into different tanks based on their breed. After partitioning, the process splits into two parallel tasks. The warehouse crew informs the administrative staff about the delivered fish, and simultaneously, they transport the fish tanks to their respective housing environments using a vehicle or forklift.

Once the administrative staff is informed, they update the fishTankTracker system with the details of the new fish. Meanwhile, the quality check officer inspects the fish tanks. If dead fish are found in any tank, the quality check officer contacts the administrative staff to arrange for disposal. The administrative staff then updates the fishTankTracker with the status of the fish tank and arranges for the disposal of the dead fish. The warehouse crew is responsible for disposing of the dead fish.

If no dead fish are found during the inspection, the administrative staff arranges for the transport of the fish when an order is received. The warehouse crew prepares the tank for delivery, and the deliveryman delivers the fish to the respective outlets, marking the end of the process.

The process begins with the system initiating the task of providing available timeslots. The system checks if a timeslot is available. If a timeslot is available, the system proceeds to gather the customer's personal information. Once the information is collected, the system books the timeslot and sends a notification to the customer. This notification is sent as a message to the customer, and the process continues with the R&D Cosmetic Specialist checking the customer's record.

If no timeslot is available, the system directs the process to a waiting period until a timeslot becomes available again, at which point the process loops back to providing available timeslots.

After the customer record is checked by the R&D Cosmetic Specialist, a decision is made based on whether the customer is new or a former customer. If the customer is new, a consult record is created. If the customer is a former customer, an existing consult record is selected. In both cases, the process continues with the R&D Cosmetic Specialist checking the customer's personal information.

Following this, the system uses outsourced software to examine the customer's skin. Based on the examination, the R&D Cosmetic Specialist advises a solution to the customer's skin problems and records the consult data. The system then updates the customer data, marking the end of the process with the consult data being updated.

The process begins with KU Leuven receiving an application. Once the application is received, KU Leuven makes an initial decision regarding the application. Following this, KU Leuven generates a PDF document. This document is then sent by KU Leuven with a request for the applicant to sign, download, or send it back. The applicant receives this request via mail.

After sending the PDF, KU Leuven waits for a specified deadline. Once the deadline is reached, KU Leuven makes a second decision on the application. This is followed by a total application decision by KU Leuven.

Next, KU Leuven evaluates the total application decision. If the application is accepted, KU Leuven reads the motivation letter and assigns a score. The complete application is then forwarded to IAAS. After forwarding, KU Leuven classifies the candidate.

At this point, KU Leuven checks if the application is unacceptable. If it is unacceptable, the application is discarded, and the process ends with the application being marked as discarded. If the application is not unacceptable, KU Leuven calculates a preference score and ranks the application.

Following the ranking, KU Leuven makes a final decision. If the application is declined, it is discarded, and the process ends with the application being marked as discarded. If the application is accepted, KU Leuven notifies the applicant via mail, and the process concludes with the application being marked as accepted.

The process begins when an academic department or research group identifies the need for vacancy approval. They wait for the scheduled meeting date to discuss the vacancy. During the meeting, the department or research group discusses the vacancy. After the discussion, they decide whether to approve or disapprove the vacancy. If they approve, they send the vacancy to the Faculty Council. If they disapprove, they adjust the vacancy and then send it to the Faculty Council.

The Faculty Council receives the vacancy and discusses it. They then decide whether to approve or disapprove the vacancy. If they disapprove, they adjust the HR policy plan and then proceed to compose an assessment committee. If they approve, they compose an assessment committee and then decide whether the vacancy is for an AAP or ZAP position. If it is an AAP position, they send the vacancy to the Staff Negotiation Committee. If it is a ZAP position, they send the vacancy to the Executive Board.

The Staff Negotiation Committee discusses the vacancy and provides non-binding advice to the Executive Board. The Executive Board then decides on the vacancy. If they approve, they notify the dean's office of the approval, and the process ends. If they disapprove, they search for an agreement with the Dean's office of the Faculty of Economics and Business Administration, and the process ends.

The process begins when a Site Engineer identifies the need for new equipment. The Site Engineer then submits a rental request. This request is received by a Clerk, who is responsible for selecting suitable equipment from the equipment catalog. Once the equipment is selected, the Clerk checks its availability.

At this point, there is a decision to be made based on the availability of the equipment. If the equipment is available, the Clerk confirms the equipment to the Works Engineer. The Works Engineer then reviews the rental request. If the request is approved, the Clerk creates a Purchase Order (PO), marking the end of the process with the PO created. If the request is rejected, the process ends with the request being rejected.

If the equipment is not available, the Clerk asks the Site Engineer to continue seeking alternatives. The Site Engineer then decides whether to continue the search process. If the Site Engineer decides to continue, they confirm this decision, and the process loops back to the Clerk selecting suitable equipment again. If the Site Engineer decides not to continue, the Clerk denies further search, and the process ends with the rental request being cancelled.

The process begins with a retailer initiating the sequence by sending a request to purchase iPhones. This request is directed to the iPhone company, which then receives the buy request. The iPhone company carefully examines the request to determine the next steps.

At this point, a decision is made by the iPhone company. There are two possible outcomes: either the merchant is found to be not accessible, or it is determined that the merchant has already filed the necessary information. If the merchant is not accessible, the iPhone company proceeds to file the merchant's information. If the merchant has already filed, the process moves forward without this step.

Following the filing of the merchant's information, or if the merchant was already filed, the iPhone company assesses the accessibility of the required requisition. Another decision point arises here. If the requisition is accessible, the iPhone company sends the iPhone requisition to the retailer. If the requisition is not accessible due to inventory issues, the iPhone company identifies that they are out of inventory and subsequently declines the requisition.

If the requisition is sent successfully, the retailer receives the iPhone shipment, marking the completion of the process. If the requisition is declined, the process also concludes, but without the shipment being sent.

The process begins with the task of checking a ULD (Unit Load Device) by the Handling Counts team. They determine if the ULD is serviceable. If it is serviceable, the ULD is returned to the pool. If it is not serviceable, the Handling Counts team scans the ULD as damaged and records this information in the JettApp system. They then proceed to count the damage.

Following the damage counting, the Handling Counts team marks the ULD based on the commission strategy, using color decals for identification. The ULD is then transported to Jetthub via a shuttle by the Jetthub team. Upon arrival, the Jetthub team unloads the ULD and performs an income scan, updating the JettApp system with the scan results.

Next, the ULD is transported to a storage rack according to the commission strategy by the Jetthub team. From the storage rack, the Rep. Shop team takes the ULD based on the commission strategy and begins the repair process. Once repaired, the ULD is moved to a parking space.

At this point, a random check is conducted by the Jetthub team. If the ULD passes the random check, it is returned to the pool. If it does not pass, the ULD is sent back to the Rep. Shop for further repairs.

If the ULD was previously repaired and sent to the parking space, the Jetthub team checks if it has been repaired. If it has been repaired, it is returned to the pool. If not, it is sent back to the Rep. Shop for additional repairs. This cycle continues until the ULD is deemed serviceable and returned to the pool.

The process begins with the Job Portal System starting the sequence by displaying the main page. An employee user then clicks the "Job Portal" button, which prompts the Job Portal System to display the relevant registration form.

The employee user proceeds to fill in the relevant data on the form. After completing this task, the employee user agrees to the terms and conditions. Once agreed, the employee user submits the registration form.

The Job Portal System then verifies the user input. At this point, there is a decision to be made based on whether the input is valid. If the input is valid, the system displays a registration confirmation message to the employee user. The employee user must then answer the confirmation message.

The Job Portal System verifies the employee user's answer. If the answer is affirmative, the system adds a new record and directs the user to the Job Seeker Main Page, concluding the process. If the answer is negative, the system cancels the registration and returns the user to the Account Main Page, ending the process.

If the initial input verification finds the input invalid, the system displays an error message and redirects the employee user back to the form to fill in the relevant data again. This loop continues until valid input is provided.

The process begins with a Sales Assistant at the CSK Production Line initiating the workflow by processing a case. The first task involves the Sales Assistant receiving a purchase order (PO).

Next, the process reaches a decision point where the Sales Assistant must determine if a payment advice has been filed. If the answer is "NO," the Sales Assistant records that no payment advice has been filed, and the process concludes with no further action required. If the answer is "YES," the Sales Assistant proceeds to have the building plans approved by the relevant authority.

Once the building plans are approved, another decision point arises. If the plans are not approved, the Sales Assistant returns the plans for changes and then rectifies them before resubmitting for approval. If the plans are approved, the Sales Assistant sends the approved plans.

Following the approval of plans, a Project Manager at the CSK Production Line creates a summary and then a work order (WO). The Project Manager then sends the WO and checks the availability of materials. This involves consulting the warehouse system to verify stock levels.

At this point, another decision is made by the Procurement team. If materials are not available, they secure materials externally from a supplier. If materials are available, the Procurement team confirms that all materials have been checked and prepares them for delivery.

Simultaneously, the Project Manager confirms the receipt of materials and makes necessary schedules. The Project Manager also confirms the finalization of the WO, which involves reviewing the WO file.

The Supervisor Line at the CSK Production Line then creates production works and approves the WO. This approval is documented in the WO file.

Throughout the process, various data objects and messages are exchanged, such as the work order file and communications with external entities like the Financial Office and Suppliers. These interactions ensure that all necessary approvals and materials are in place for the production line to proceed efficiently.

The business process begins with the reception of raw materials by the Leather Production team, led by Jane Doe. Once the raw materials are received, they are selected for quality by the same team. After selection, the process waits for the arrival of the customer order and its specific requirements. Once these requirements are received, the Leather Production team proceeds with re-tanning the leather.

Following re-tanning, the leather undergoes dressing, and then physical tests are conducted to ensure quality. After passing the physical tests, the leather is selected based on the cutting requirements specified by the customer. The selected leather is then packaged and shipped by the Leather Production team.

Simultaneously, the Cutting team, also managed by Jane Doe, sets up the necessary equipment and processes for cutting. After setup, they proceed with nesting, which involves arranging the materials for optimal cutting. Once nesting is complete, the cutting task is performed. The cut materials are then packaged and shipped.

After shipping, a decision point is reached where it is determined whether printing is requested. If printing is requested, the Printing team, under Jane Doe's supervision, sets up for printing. They then perform digital printing, followed by packaging and shipping of the printed materials.

If printing is not requested, the process moves directly to the final quality control conducted by the Leather Production team. If the customer quality control is satisfactory, the leather is packaged and shipped. Finally, the order is closed, marking the end of the process. Throughout the process, customer requirements are referenced to ensure all tasks meet the specified needs.

The process begins when the Frontliners identify that a request is needed. They start by selecting the type of request they want to make. Once the request type is selected, the Frontliners proceed to submit the request.

After the request is submitted, Mitra from the Retail Operation receives an email notification about the new request. Mitra then reviews the request to determine its outcome. At this point, there is a decision to be made: if the request is approved, Mitra will proceed to approve the request. If the request is rejected, Mitra will reject the request.

If Mitra approves the request, the Frontliners receive an email notification informing them of the approval. This leads to the next step where the Admin HQ Retail Support & Retail receives an email notification about the approved request. The Admin HQ Retail Support & Retail then reviews the request again. They also have a decision to make: if they approve the request, they proceed to approve it, and the Frontliners receive an approval email notification. If they reject the request, the Frontliners receive a rejection email notification. In both cases, the process ends for the Frontliners.

If Mitra rejects the request, the Frontliners receive a rejection email notification, and the process ends with the request being marked as rejected. 

Throughout the process, each actor is responsible for specific tasks, and the flow of information is managed through email notifications, ensuring that all parties are informed of the request's status at each stage.

The process begins with students initiating the application procedure by filling in an online form. Once the form is completed, students submit it online. After submission, students are required to print and sign the PDF document generated from the form. They then post this signed PDF document along with any necessary attachments to the GG Institute of Arts.

Upon receiving the documents, a staff member or clerk at the institute checks the completeness of the submitted documents. If the documents are incomplete, the staff member sends an email notification to the student, informing them of the missing documents. The student must then post the missing documents to the institute.

If the documents are complete, the process moves forward to the executive of the admission office, who verifies the validity of the certified documents. If the documents are not valid, the executive sends a rejection notification by email, and the process ends with the application being rejected.

If the documents are valid, the process continues with the academic committee, who decides on the admission offer. The committee then meets and evaluates the participant. Following this evaluation, the committee generates a list of successful and unsuccessful applications.

Finally, the executive of the admission office sends an outcome notification by email to the applicants, informing them of the result of their application. The process concludes with this notification.

The business process begins with a Business User initiating the process. The Business User sends a change request to the Tier 1 manager. Once the request is received, the Tier 1 agent evaluates the change ticket and sets a priority level for it. After setting the priority, the Tier 1 agent alerts a Tier 2 agent to look into the issue.

At this point, the process reaches a decision point handled by Tier 2. The Tier 2 agent assesses whether they can resolve the issue themselves. If the Tier 2 agent can resolve the issue, they proceed to perform the necessary changes. After completing the changes, the Tier 2 agent informs the Tier 1 agent about the rectification.

If the Tier 2 agent cannot resolve the issue, they escalate it to Tier 3. The Tier 3 agent then performs the required changes. Following the changes, Tier 3 conducts testing to ensure everything is functioning correctly. After successful testing, Tier 3 informs the Tier 1 agent and requests them to inform the Business User about the changes.

Once the Tier 1 agent is informed of the rectification, they notify the Deputy about the resolution. The Business User then acknowledges the rectification and instructs the Tier 1 agent to close the case. Finally, the Tier 1 agent changes the status of the case from open to closed, marking the end of the process.

The process begins with a student who is interested in studying abroad for a master's degree. The student starts by searching for a suitable location for their master's studies. Once the location search is complete, the student reaches a decision point where they must choose between three countries: the UK, the USA, or Germany.

If the student chooses Germany, they proceed to select Germany as their destination due to the benefit of free education. Following this decision, the student searches for the requirements needed to study in Germany. Next, the student looks for courses, focusing on course choice and ensuring the course language is English. After selecting a course, the student searches for universities offering the chosen course.

At this point, the student encounters another decision point where they must choose between applying to a public university or a private university. If the student opts for a public university, they then search for the specific requirements needed for that university.

Once the university requirements are identified, the IT department, on behalf of the study abroad program, applies and sends the necessary documents. After the documents are sent, the student proceeds to get admission to the chosen university.

Following admission, the student reaches another decision point. Here, they must decide whether to block a certain amount of funds. If they choose to block the amount, they then prepare the necessary visa requirements. After preparing the visa requirements, the student applies for a visa.

While waiting for visa acceptance, the student looks for accommodation options, such as a student dormitory or a private shared apartment (WG). Once the visa is accepted, the student can proceed to buy a ticket to Germany, facilitated by the IT department.

After purchasing the ticket, the student prepares a list of things to take to Germany as a student. Upon arrival in Germany, the student registers their address. Following the address registration, the student completes the enrollment process at the university.

The process concludes with the student starting their course, marking the end of the preparation and transition phase for studying abroad.

The process begins when a junior medical consultant at Mental Health Plus receives a call from a person. The consultant's first task is to determine whether the situation is an emergency. If it is deemed an emergency, the consultant instructs the caller to hang up and dial 111, ending the call.

If the situation is not an emergency, the consultant asks the caller to provide their name, contact details, and symptoms. This information is then confirmed by a psychologist, who decides whether the caller needs to see a specialist.

If a specialist is needed, the psychologist provides the caller with the contact details of the specialist, and the call ends. If no specialist is needed, the psychologist assesses the severity of the caller's mental health issue.

If the issue is not severe, the psychologist provides the caller with exercises to improve their mood, and the call ends. If the issue is severe, the psychologist conveys this information to the caller and looks up a suitable time and date for a consultation.

Finally, the psychologist provides the caller with the time, date, and address for the consultation, concluding the process.

The business process begins when an online order is received by the information system. Once the order is received, the information system sends an order confirmation email to the customer.

Next, the order fulfillment department, led by Mighty Jane Doe, packs the product in a package. After packing, the department checks if bubble protection is required for the shipment. This decision is made by evaluating whether the package needs additional protection.

If bubble protection is needed, the order fulfillment department adds bubble protection to the package. Once this is done, or if no bubble protection is required, the package is handed over to the warehouse.

The warehouse staff, also under the supervision of Mighty Jane Doe, then checks if the customer has chosen normal post or fast courier for delivery. This decision determines the next steps in the process.

If the customer selected normal post, the warehouse staff fills in the post label. If the customer opted for fast courier, the staff gets a quote from the contracted courier and prepares the necessary courier paperwork.

After either the post label is filled or the courier paperwork is prepared, the warehouse staff combines the appropriate documentation with the package. This marks the end of the process, with the paperwork and package ready for dispatch.

The process begins when a business owner identifies a need. The business owner then submits a dashboard form outlining their request. PfizerWorks reviews the form, engages with the customer, and explores the request. Following this, the Analytics Solution Delivery team shares and consults with their team to vet the request.

PfizerWorks collects data requests and provides a t-shirt estimate back to the customer. The business owner then determines whether the request remains viable and desirable. If the decision is to continue, the customer submits a request to HRIS Data Governance. If not, the process ends.

HRIS reviews the request and decides whether to approve or deny it. If denied, the business owner is alerted on how to remediate or close the request. If approved, an entry is made in the HR Data Tracker, and approval is granted. The customer then moves to the full Statement of Work (SOW) process.

PfizerWorks begins the formal SOW creation process, and the Analytics Solution Delivery team performs full vetting and governance, contributing to the SOW and costs. PfizerWorks finalizes the SOW and shares it with the customer, who then makes a decision on the SOW. If the customer signs the SOW, the project launches. If not, the process ends.

Once the project is launched, PfizerWorks ensures it is ready to move to production. HRIS confirms that all approvals and governance are in place. The Analytics Solution Delivery team confirms testing and documentation. PfizerWorks then moves the project to production, and the business owner confirms acceptance, closing the project.

The process begins with Jane Doe, a member of the Accreditation Team, starting the workflow. She receives an email notification indicating approval. Following this, Jane Doe determines whether the information is already present in Swim Central.

At this point, there is a decision to be made. If the information is not in Swim Central, Jane Doe fills in a spreadsheet. After completing the spreadsheet, she sends an email to Julie S. This email is an intermediate step, and Jane Doe waits to receive the completed spreadsheet back. Once she receives it, she copies the data into the Swim Central template, adds a security stamp, and imports the data into the Swim Central CRM. After the import is complete, Jane Doe is notified of the completion, and the process loops back to allocate membership products.

If the information is already in Swim Central, Jane Doe proceeds to allocate membership products. This step is associated with the "years of accreditation" annotation. After allocating membership products, Jane Doe allocates accreditations. Following this, she emails a certificate using the Accreditation email template. This marks the end of the process, completing the workflow.

The process begins when the customer opens the app for the first time. The customer then clicks on the option to start a new application. Following this, the customer selects a mooring location.

Next, the customer encounters a decision point where they must identify themselves as either an organization or an individual. If the customer selects "organization," they proceed to fill out the organization form. If they select "individual," they fill out the individual form. Both paths lead to another decision point where the customer must choose between "unrestricted" and "restricted" options.

If the customer chooses "unrestricted," they enter the type of business and provide a brief description of the intended purpose of the mooring. They also specify the maximum length of the expected mooring ships. If the customer chooses "restricted," they provide details about the ship, including its name, registration, length overall (LOA), make/design, color, draft, and engine size. Both paths converge to a task where the customer provides buoy mooring details, such as block weight, dimensions, material, chain length, and coordinates (latitude and longitude).

The customer then uploads a photo, document, or a current Queensland certificate of registration. Following this, they tick a box to confirm that a cultural heritage assessment has been completed, with a reference to the cultural heritage website.

Next, the customer extracts a chart and uploads written approval from relevant entities if the proposed buoy moorings are affected by policies. They then create a profile and provide personal details.

The customer ticks a box to declare acceptance of terms and conditions, with a reference to the terms and conditions document. They then enter their email and password, fill out their Customer Reference Number (CRN), and confirm their email, with a reference to the CRN website.

Finally, the customer proceeds to the payment process. Once completed, the application is sent to the admin portal, concluding the process.

The process begins with an employee who needs a vacation. The employee starts by checking their remaining holiday days. After verifying the available days, the employee checks the data in the HR system to ensure accuracy. Once the data is confirmed, the employee sends an email to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) with the start and end dates of the requested vacation.

The CEO receives the email and reads it. Following this, the CEO checks the system data in the HR system to verify the request. After confirming the data, the CEO reviews the project plans to assess the impact of the employee's absence. Once the project plans are checked, the CEO sends an email back to the employee with the decision regarding the vacation request.

The employee receives the email from the CEO and reads it. If the vacation is approved, the employee confirms the vacation and updates their calendar accordingly. This confirmation triggers two simultaneous actions: the employee reads another email from the CEO, and the CEO books the holiday in the HR system. 

Once the holiday is booked, the CEO updates the project plans to reflect the employee's absence. Simultaneously, the HR system is updated with the new vacation information. The process concludes with the employee updating their calendar, marking the end of the vacation request process.

The process begins when the accounting department receives an invoice. The first task for the accounting department is to send the invoice to the business unit. Once the business unit receives the invoice, they proceed to approve it.

At this point, the business unit faces a decision. They must determine whether the invoice is approved or not. If the invoice is not approved, the business unit informs the accounting department, which then informs the supplier that the invoice is unapproved, concluding this branch of the process.

If the invoice is approved, the business unit sends the approved invoice back to the accounting department. Upon receiving the approved invoice, the accounting department fills in the necessary accounting information onto the invoice.

Following this, the process splits into two parallel tasks. The accounting department simultaneously proceeds to pay the supplier and updates the accounts payable records. Once both tasks are completed, the process concludes with the invoice being marked as paid.

The process begins with the applicant initiating the procedure by applying online for admission to the university. After submitting the online application, the applicant is required to forward the necessary documents through postal mail.

Once the documents are sent, the admission office receives them and proceeds to review the data contained within these files. After the review, the admission office forwards the files to the department of informatics for further assessment.

The department of informatics receives the files and evaluates whether the applicant meets the admission standards. At this point, a decision is made. If the applicant does not meet the standards, the department refuses the candidate's selection and issues a letter of refusal. This letter is then sent to the applicant.

If the applicant meets the standards, the department sends an appeal letter inviting the applicant for an interview. The applicant is expected to attend the interview, which is conducted by the department of informatics. Following the interview, the department selects the candidate and sends a notification of selection to the applicant.

The process concludes with the applicant receiving either a refusal letter or a notification of selection, depending on the outcome of the assessment and interview.

The process begins when Jane Doe has candies ready to be sold either in a supermarket or online. Jane Doe is responsible for this initial step.

Next, Jane Doe chooses the candies as per the client's preference. After making a choice, Jane Doe proceeds to the next step.

Jane Doe then unboxes the package of candies. Following this, she checks the appearance of each candy to ensure they meet the expected standards.

At this point, Jane Doe evaluates whether the appearance of the candies is satisfactory. If the appearance is good, she moves on to taste the candies. If the appearance is not satisfactory, she sends the candies back and requests a refund or a change.

If Jane Doe finds the appearance satisfactory and proceeds to taste the candies, she then decides if the taste is good. If the taste is good, she decides to buy the candies again next time. If the taste is not good, she decides to try a different type of candy next time.

If Jane Doe decides to send the candies back due to unsatisfactory appearance, the retailers send the candies back to the manufacturer. The process then involves finding the responsible departments and individuals for the issue. Penalties are imposed on the related companies and individuals involved.

The process concludes with either Jane Doe deciding to purchase the candies again, trying a different candy next time, or the resolution of the complaint through penalties.

The process begins when the vehicle owner arrives at the designated lane with their vehicle. The vehicle owner then exits the vehicle. Following this, the vehicle owner receives a request for the keys. The vehicle owner hands over the keys to the inspector, which is communicated through a message. After this, the vehicle owner waits to receive a notification about the completion of the inspection.

Simultaneously, the inspection center starts its process once the customer has left the vehicle. The inspection center checks if the keys are inside the vehicle. If the keys are not found, the inspection center informs the customer, and the process loops back to the point where the vehicle owner receives a request for the keys. If the keys are present, the inspection center picks up the keys and starts the engine.

The inspection center then proceeds to inspect the vehicle at three different bases: Base 2, Base 3, and Base 4. After completing the inspections at all bases, the inspection center notifies the customer that the inspection is complete. This notification is sent as a message to the vehicle owner.

The vehicle owner, upon receiving the notification, proceeds to pick up the vehicle along with the completed inspection document. This marks the end of the vehicle owner's part of the process, indicating that the vehicle inspection is completed.

Meanwhile, the inspection center records the inspection results. Once the results are recorded, this marks the end of the inspection center's part of the process, indicating that the inspection results have been successfully documented.

The process begins with a pharmacist at the pharmacy initiating the workflow. A customer requests a prescription, and the pharmacist takes note of this request. Following this, the pharmacist asks the customer a series of administrative questions to gather necessary information.

Next, the pharmacist checks if the customer's history is already present in the system. This involves accessing the Customer Master Data. The process then reaches a decision point where the pharmacist determines if the customer is already in the system. If the customer is not in the system, the pharmacist inputs the new customer details. If the customer is already in the system, the pharmacist selects the existing customer profile.

After handling the customer profile, the pharmacist selects or inputs the doctor's details and the required branded medications. This step involves referencing the Inventory Master Data and the Prescriber Master Data to ensure accuracy.

The pharmacist then verifies if the requested products are in stock by consulting the Item Master Data. This leads to another decision point: if the product is not in stock, the pharmacist notifies the customer, and the process ends. If the product is in stock, the pharmacist retrieves the product from the store's stock area.

Once the product is retrieved, the pharmacist scans it into the system and prints a script label. The script label is generated as a document output. The pharmacist then verifies that the product matches the required prescription medication.

If the patient's prescription is new, the pharmacist prints off drug information for the customer. This step involves accessing the Vendor Master Data. Finally, the pharmacist finalizes the prescription with the customer, concluding the process. The process ends with the pharmacist completing the transaction with the customer.

The process begins when a customer places an order using either a card or the Snoonu Wallet. Once the order is placed, the next step involves a transaction where the bank holds an authorization for the payment. This transaction is also initiated by the customer.

After the transaction, the order is processed and confirmed by both the vendor and Snoonu. Once confirmed, a message is sent indicating that the order is ready for pickup. This task is handled by the finance team at Snoonu.

Following this, there is a decision point managed by Snoonu's finance team. If the order is successful, a notification is sent to the fleet dashboard indicating that the order is on the way. This notification is handled by the driver. Subsequently, the bank deducts the money, and the payment is received by Snoonu's finance team, leading to the fulfillment of the order.

If the order is canceled, a cancellation notification along with the reason is sent to the fleet dashboard. This task is also managed by Snoonu's finance team. Following the cancellation, the transaction is reversed in real time by the finance team.

After the transaction reversal, another decision point occurs. If a credit card was used, the money is returned to the bank account or card. If the Snoonu Wallet or a debit card was used, the amount is credited back to the Snoonu Wallet. Both these tasks are handled by Snoonu's finance team.

Finally, whether the payment is received or reversed, the process concludes with the order being fulfilled. This marks the end of the process, managed by Snoonu's finance team.

The business process begins with a sales employee initiating the process. The first task for the sales employee is to process a request for service. Once this is completed, the sales employee moves on to check the business opportunity.

After the business opportunity check, there is a decision point. If the business cannot be done, the sales employee will reject the engagement, leading to the end of the process. If the business opportunity is viable, the sales employee will define what services can be delivered.

Following the definition of deliverable services, another decision point occurs. If the services cannot be delivered, the sales employee will reject the engagement, ending the process. If the services can be delivered, the sales employee assigns a consultant or risk assessor.

Once a consultant or risk assessor is assigned, they are responsible for making a proposal. After the proposal is made, it is sent to strategic management for approval. If approved, the consultant or risk assessor presents the proposal.

After presenting the proposal, there is another decision point. If the proposal is rejected, the sales employee will reject the engagement, ending the process. If the proposal is chosen, the consultant or risk assessor proceeds to do the project.

Upon completion of the project, the consultant or risk assessor provides aftercare services. Finally, the process concludes with the consultant or risk assessor marking the end of the process.

The process begins with students uploading their resumes. Once the resume is uploaded, students are asked if they have any existing problems. If there are no problems, students proceed to search for full-time jobs or internships. After searching, the teaching and administrative staff provide referrals for qualified students.

If students have existing problems, they are directed to the CUCP portal site to process frequently asked questions. If further assistance is needed, they can ask for help from the IT service desk.

After receiving referrals, students apply for jobs or internships. Once applications are submitted, students evaluate if the applied position is relevant. If the position is not relevant, the system places restrictions on the application, ending the process. If the position is relevant, the application proceeds.

The company then reviews the application to determine if it is selected. If not selected, the system receives a rejection, and students are notified of the rejection. If selected, the system receives a selection notification, and students receive an email with selection details and interview information.

Students attend the interview, and the company conducts an interview screening. The system then receives the selection decisions. Students are informed of the selection results through mail. If not selected, the process ends. If selected, students contact CUCP for detailed queries, and the CUCP portal site sends an inmail.

The process begins with the reader initiating the subscription order by visiting the website www.katyd.cz. Once on the website, the reader is presented with a form to enter basic information such as their name and address. After the form is displayed, the reader fills it out with the necessary details.

Following the completion of the form, the reader is faced with a decision regarding the method of payment. If the reader chooses to pay offline, they are shown the payment information by www.katyd.cz. This leads to the payment being processed by Media Servis. After the payment is processed, Media Servis determines the variant of the subscription. If the subscription is only for print, the process ends. If the subscription includes online access or both online and print, Media Servis generates a code for the reader.

The reader then enters this code back on the website www.katyd.cz, which results in the assignment of subscription rights to the reader, concluding the process.

Alternatively, if the reader opts for online payment, the payment is processed by GoPay. Once the payment is processed, the reader is asked to choose the variant of the subscription. If the subscription includes online access or both online and print, the reader is assigned subscription rights on the website www.katyd.cz, and the process ends. If the subscription is only for print, Media Servis registers the payment information for accounting and renews the subscription, which also concludes the process.

The process begins when someone realizes they need coffee after feeling sleepy at their desk. The Kitchen department is responsible for executing the following tasks to make coffee using a Moka pot.

First, the Kitchen department takes the Moka pot out of the cupboard. Next, they dismantle the Moka pot into its separate parts. Following this, they fill up the kettle with water.

Once the kettle is filled, two tasks occur simultaneously. The Kitchen department takes out the coffee from the cupboard and puts it in the middle part of the Moka pot. At the same time, they turn on the kettle to boil the water. After the water boils, it is poured into the water reservoir of the Moka pot.

With the coffee in place and the water ready, the Kitchen department puts all the parts of the Moka pot together and places it on the stove. Simultaneously, they turn the stove on to start brewing the coffee.

While the coffee is brewing, the Kitchen department takes the milk out of the fridge and retrieves a mug from the cupboard. Once the coffee starts to boil and rise in the Moka pot, they remove it from the stove.

The brewed coffee is then poured into the mug. The Kitchen department adds sugar to the coffee, followed by milk. Finally, they stir the coffee to mix all the ingredients.

The process concludes with the person enjoying their freshly made coffee and getting back to work, feeling refreshed and alert.

The process begins when a student decides to make changes to their resume. The student starts by editing their resume. Once the editing is complete, the student emails the draft to the Communications Manager.

Simultaneously, another process starts when a resume email is sent out. The student receives an email asking for their resume. The student then decides whether they will attend a job fair. If the student chooses not to attend, they notify the Communications Manager that they will not be attending. The Communications Manager then notes that the student is not attending, and no further work is required.

If the student decides to attend the job fair, they proceed to create their resume. After creating the resume, the student edits it and emails the draft to the Communications Manager.

Upon receiving the resume draft, the Communications Manager updates an Excel document with a timestamp. The Communications Manager then saves and opens the resume to review it. At this point, the Communications Manager checks if the student followed the directions.

If the student did not follow the directions, the Communications Manager emails the student to start over. The student receives this email and begins the process of editing the resume again.

If the student followed the directions, the Communications Manager edits the resume as needed. After editing, the Communications Manager saves the resume to a "done" folder with a new file name. The Communications Manager then emails the approved resume back to the student.

Finally, the Communications Manager updates an Excel sheet with the timestamp of the approval, marking the end of the process as the student is done.

The process begins with an employee who wants to get their expenses reimbursed. The employee initiates the process by filling out a reimbursement request. Once the request is completed, the employee sends it to their manager for examination.

The manager examines the request and decides whether to approve or reject it. If the manager rejects the request, it is sent back to the employee to be filled out again. If the manager approves the request, it is forwarded to the expense reimbursement team.

The expense reimbursement team examines the report. If they find no errors, they send the report to the finance department via email. If there are issues with the report, the expense reimbursement team rejects it, and it is sent back to the employee to be filled out again.

Once the finance department receives the report, they initiate the reimbursement process. This marks the end of the process.

The process begins when goods arrive at the storage space. The Storage Admin is responsible for this initial step. Upon arrival, the Storage Admin uses a tablet camera to scan the delivery note. This action leads to the next step, where the ScannerSys IoT captures the details on the delivery note. Once the details are captured, ScannerSys IoT records them into the Warehouse Inventory System (WIS).

Following the recording of details, the Storage Admin pastes an RFID sticker on the goods. After this, the Storage Admin uses the tablet to call the RoboMover to the pickup location. The RoboMover IoT then checks the type of goods on the Warehouse Inventory System.

At this point, a decision is made by the RoboMover IoT regarding whether the goods need refrigeration. If the goods do not require refrigeration, the RoboMover IoT moves them to the dry storage area. If refrigeration is needed, the RoboMover IoT moves the goods to the cold storage.

After the goods are moved to the appropriate storage area, the SKU Vault IoT checks the location of expiring goods. This information is used by the Storage Admin to assign a location for the new goods based on the expiring goods. The RoboMover IoT then sends the goods to empty shelves and updates the shelf details, marking the end of the process.

The process begins when the insurance company receives a claim. The company then evaluates whether the claim is reasonable. If the claim seems suspicious, the insurance company contacts a third-party company to verify the claim. The third-party company inspects the claim and informs the insurance company about the outcome.

If the claim is deemed admissible, the insurance company transfers the money to the customer's bank account. The customer is then informed via email that the claim will shortly be reimbursed, concluding the process for the customer.

If the third-party company informs the insurance company that the claim should be rejected, the customer is informed by letter, and the process ends for the customer. If the third-party company suggests that the claim might be fraudulent, an insurance employee makes a decision. The employee can either forward the case to the fraud department or decide to reject the claim. If forwarded, a report is generated and sent to the fraud department, which then starts its work.

Throughout this process, the insurance company ensures that each step is carefully evaluated, and appropriate actions are taken based on the information received from the third-party company and internal assessments.

The process begins when the cashier of the tribunal receives a compensation request. The first step involves the cashier retrieving the premises file. Once the file is retrieved, the cashier checks the filing file.

At this point, a decision is made based on the completeness of the filing file. If the file is complete, the cashier proceeds to check the compliant file. If the file is incomplete, the cashier rejects the file, and the process ends with the file being marked as rejected.

If the compliant file is checked and found to be complete, the cashier accepts both the filing and compliant files and sets a hearing date. If the compliant file is incomplete, the cashier rejects the file, and the process ends with the file being marked as rejected.

After setting a hearing date, the cashier evaluates whether any fees are required. If fees are required and not paid, the cashier produces a fees notice and waits for the owner to pay. If additional fees are paid, or if the required fees are already paid, the cashier generates a receipt and allocates a hearing date.

Once the hearing date is allocated, the process concludes successfully. If the owner pays the fees after receiving the notice, the cashier reassesses the compliance document, and the process ends with the document being reassessed.

The process begins when an order is received by the shipping process of the Shipping Company. The first task is to register the order, which is handled by the shipping process team.

Once the order is registered, the process reaches a decision point. Here, the shipping process can take one of two paths. The first path involves emailing the client, while the second path involves checking the client's address. Both tasks are managed by the shipping process team.

After either emailing the client or checking the client's address, the next step is to send the designated driver. This task is also carried out by the shipping process team.

Following this, the process encounters another decision point. Again, there are two possible paths. The first path involves creating a list of shipping boxes, and the second path involves checking the client's address once more. Both tasks are performed by the shipping process team.

Once either the list of shipping boxes is created or the client's address is checked, the car is loaded with the shipment. This task is managed by the shipping process team.

After the car is loaded, the driver leaves to deliver the shipment. This task is also handled by the shipping process team.

Next, the shipping process team calls the client to inform them about the delivery.

The process continues with the client receiving the shipment, which is managed by the shipping process team.

Finally, the process concludes when the driver confirms the shipping, marking the end of the process.

The business process begins with the BAS actor opening the BAS system. Once the BAS system is open, the BAS actor makes changes to the code. After making the necessary code changes, the BAS actor increases the version number in the MTA.yaml file. Following this, the BAS actor creates a Multi Target Application (MTA) archive.

At this point, a decision is made by the BAS actor on whether to deploy the application to the development environment. If the decision is "YES," the process moves to another decision point where the BAS actor decides if it is the first deployment or if it should be done via the Command Line Interface (CLI). If the decision is "YES," the BAS actor enters the information of the deployment environment. After entering the deployment information, the BAS actor proceeds to deploy the application manually. This leads to the end of the process with the application being deployed.

If the decision to deploy to the development environment is "NO," the process shifts to the Cloud Transport Management actor. The Cloud Transport Management actor downloads the Multi Target Application Archive. After downloading, the Cloud Transport Management actor opens the Cloud Transport Management Service. The actor then navigates to the desired node, which could be either QA or PROD. Following this, the Cloud Transport Management actor adds an entry to the import queue. The next step involves uploading the MTA to the entry. Once the MTA is uploaded, the Cloud Transport Management actor waits for the hourly import to occur. This concludes the process with the application being deployed.

The process begins when a student initiates a request. This request is made through the Wreck Techs Website. Once the request is initiated, the ERP-System creates or updates and stores a ticket for the issue.

Next, a technician from Wreck Techs reads the request. After reviewing the request, the technician determines whether the issue is related to the network or the device. This decision point leads to two possible paths:

1. If the issue is identified as a network problem, the technician evaluates the network strength in the room. Following this evaluation, the ERP-System updates the ticket with the network evaluation results. The technician then decides on the appropriate action for the issue.

2. If the issue is identified as a device problem, the technician suggests quick solutions to the student. The ERP-System updates and stores the ticket with this information. The student then attempts to apply the suggested solutions.

If the student successfully resolves the issue, they confirm to the technician that the solution works, and the technician closes the ticket. If the student cannot resolve the issue, they notify the technician of the results. The ERP-System updates and stores the ticket again, and the technician advises the student to bring the device to the Helpdesk.

Once the student brings the device to the Helpdesk, the technician confirms the decision to the student, and the ticket is closed.

If the technician decides on an issue action that requires further processing, a parallel process begins. The ERP-System manages the queue to respond to the lead technician's request, and the technician informs the student of the decision. Both actions lead to the ticket being forwarded to the ITG, concluding the process.

The process begins when a client makes contact. The client then registers the required information, which is stored in a data repository labeled "Provided online services." After registering, the client books an appointment with a dietician.

Once the appointment is booked, the dietician confirms the booking. If the booking is confirmed, two actions occur simultaneously: the dietician sends a confirmation letter to the client, and the client can make use of other provided services. The confirmation letter is documented as a "Confirmation letter."

If the booking is not confirmed, the client must book the appointment again.

After the confirmation letter is sent and the client uses other services, the dietician starts the meeting. During the meeting, the dietician suggests a treatment plan. Following this, the dietician books an evaluation meeting.

Once the meeting is finished, the client is instructed to keep a diary for evaluation purposes. The evaluation meeting is then held by the dietician. After the evaluation, the dietician keeps in contact with the client, marking the end of the process.

The process begins with the Principal initiating the procedure. The first step involves the Principal inviting participants to a meeting. Following this, the Principal conducts the first meeting.

After the meeting, the Principal reaches a decision point. Here, there are two possible paths. The first path is if the Principal decides not to proceed, leading to the task of agreeing not to proceed. This decision results in moving to the next suspect, which concludes the process.

The second path is if the Principal agrees to provide a quote. This decision leads to the Administrator or Practice Manager collecting basic information. During this task, a thank you letter is generated, and a questionnaire or checklist of required information is prepared.

Once the basic information is collected, the process continues with a Professional Specialist drafting a proposal. The drafted proposal is then discussed and authorized by the Principal.

Another decision point follows. If the proposal needs revision, the Principal revises it, and then it is authorized again. Once authorized, the proposal is sent, marking the end of this path in the process. If no revisions are needed, the proposal is sent directly after authorization, concluding the process.

The process begins when a customer initiates a service request. The customer then submits a special request, which is communicated as a special service request to an employee.

The employee registers the service request and checks if the requested service is available. If the service is available, the employee determines if there are additional charges associated with the service. If there are no additional charges, the employee assesses whether the service can be fulfilled by a hotel employee. If it can, the employee sends a service request confirmation to the customer and proceeds to provide the service, completing the process with the customer's special request being fulfilled.

If the service incurs additional charges, the employee calculates the total cost and adds the charge to the final invoice before reassessing if the service can be fulfilled by a hotel employee. If the service cannot be fulfilled by a hotel employee, the employee coordinates with an external service provider, sending the service request details to them. The external service provider then communicates back to the employee, who sends a service request confirmation to the customer.

If the requested service is not available, the employee rejects the customer's request and informs the customer of the rejection. The customer then accepts the service request rejection, concluding the process with the customer's special request being rejected.

The process begins when a customer enters the Italian restaurant. The restaurant staff then asks the customer if they would like to see the menu. After receiving the menu, the customer checks the available offers.

Once the offers are reviewed, the process splits into two simultaneous actions. The customer orders a glass of red wine and a salad at the same time. After placing these orders, the customer waits for the order to be prepared.

When the order is ready, the customer receives the salad and wine. The customer then enjoys the salad and drinks the wine.

After finishing the meal, the customer is asked if they would like to order dessert. At this point, the customer has a choice to make. If the customer decides to order tiramisu, they place the order and wait for it to be prepared. Once the tiramisu is ready, the customer receives it and enjoys the dessert. After finishing the tiramisu, the customer asks for the bill.

If the customer decides not to order tiramisu, they directly ask for the bill without ordering any dessert.

Once the bill is requested, the customer pays it. Finally, after settling the bill, the customer leaves the restaurant, concluding the process.

The process begins when Jerry's House has the goods ready. Jerry's House then informs the warehouse about the readiness of the goods. After informing the warehouse, Jerry's House checks the delivery requirements. At this point, there is a decision to be made: if a special carrier is needed, the process moves to the clerk to ask for a quotation. If a normal delivery is sufficient, the clerk checks if extra insurance is necessary.

If the clerk determines that extra insurance is necessary, the process moves to the Logistics Manager, who provides the extra insurance. Once the extra insurance is provided, or if it was determined that no extra insurance is needed, the clerk prepares the necessary paperwork.

After preparing the paperwork, the clerk gives it to the warehouse. The warehouse then receives the paperwork and adds it to the packaged goods. Once the paperwork is added, the warehouse moves the goods to the pick-up area. Finally, the process concludes when the goods are picked up from the warehouse.

The process begins when a customer realizes they need groceries. The customer then goes to the Costco app and adds the desired items to their cart. After adding items, the customer checks for available delivery slots. If a delivery slot is available, the customer selects it and proceeds to make the payment using a credit or debit card. If no delivery slots are available, the process ends with no grocery delivery.

Once the payment is made, an Instacart shopper is assigned to the order. The shopper begins shopping for the items. As the shopper shops, they check if each item is available. If an item is found, it is placed in the cart. If an item is not found, the customer is notified via text with a replacement option. The customer then decides whether to accept the replacement. If the customer accepts, the process continues with the replacement item. If the customer does not accept, the item is canceled, and a refund is processed.

After all items are placed in the cart, the Instacart shopper verifies that everything is correct. The shopper then proceeds to the checkout, where a Costco checkout agent scans all the items in the cart. Following this, the checkout agent scans the Instacart payment card. The Instacart shopper then shows the checkout receipt, and the process concludes with the groceries being delivered to the customer.

The process begins when the loan provider receives an application. The first step is to determine whether the application is approved. If the application is not approved, the loan provider notifies the applicant about the rejection, and the process ends with the application being rejected.

If the application is approved, the loan provider sends a proposal for home insurance to the applicant. The applicant then receives the offer of home insurance and decides whether they are interested in it. If the applicant is interested, they inform the loan provider, who then sends an acceptance pack to the applicant. If the applicant is not interested, the loan provider sends both an acceptance pack and the home insurance to the applicant.

Once the applicant receives the acceptance pack, with or without the home insurance, the loan provider verifies the repayment agreement. After this verification, the process concludes.

The process begins with the requester starting the procedure. The requester then fills out a request form, which includes creating a position description document. After completing the form, the manager reviews and approves the request. If the request is approved, the process continues; if not, the process is canceled.

Once approved, the human resources team searches for candidates in a resume database. Simultaneously, they post the position and wait for resumes to arrive. The resumes are collected as a document. The requester then analyzes the resumes and selects potential candidates.

At this point, a decision is made by the requester: if suitable candidates are found, the human resources team invites them for interviews and applies tests. If no suitable candidates are found, the process returns to posting the position and waiting for more resumes.

After the tests and interviews, the requester conducts further interviews with the candidates. Following this, the human resources team selects the final candidates. They then finalize the recruitment process and contact the selected individuals. Finally, the candidate is hired, and the process concludes.

The process begins with the Sales Team accepting a sales opportunity. They start by checking the details of the sales and the customer's information to ensure everything is correct. This task is performed by the Sales Team and involves verifying the accuracy of the information.

Once the details are confirmed, the Sales Team requests a new contract for the customer. This request leads to the Legal Team generating a contract based on a template and the sales information stored in Salesforce. The Legal Team then reviews the contract to ensure it meets all necessary requirements.

After the review, the Legal Team uploads the contract and generates a DocuSign link using the DocuSign API. This step involves two simultaneous actions: the Legal Team informs the Sales Team that the DocuSign link has been generated, and the DocuSign API sends the link to the customer.

The customer receives the link and proceeds to sign the contract. If the contract is signed, the DocuSign API notifies the Sales Team that the contract has been signed. If the contract is not signed within three days, a reminder is sent to the customer to sign the contract.

Once the contract is signed, the Sales Team marks the opportunity as closed in Salesforce. They then thank the customer and ask for feedback. The customer provides feedback, and the process concludes with the deal being officially closed.

The process begins when a customer requests a vaccination at the pharmacy. The front desk staff initiates the process by conducting a pre-vaccination screening to ensure the customer is eligible for the vaccine. If the customer passes the screening, the front desk checks the validity of the customer's consent. Once confirmed, the front desk copies the customer's Medicare card and identification card.

Next, the pharmacist prepares the necessary equipment for the vaccination. After the equipment is ready, the pharmacist prepares the customer to receive the vaccine. The pharmacist then administers the vaccine to the customer.

Following the injection, the pharmacist monitors the customer's condition to ensure there are no immediate adverse reactions. If no adverse events occur, the pharmacist informs the customer of any necessary precautions after receiving the vaccine. If an adverse event does occur, the pharmacist provides rapid medical care to address the situation.

After the vaccination process, the front desk documents the vaccine in the customer's medical record and records the administration in the AIR system. The front desk then handles the billing process to complete the transaction.

If the customer does not pass the initial screening, the front desk makes an appointment for the customer to return for a future service. This concludes the process for customers who are not immediately eligible for vaccination.

Finally, the process ends with the completion of the vaccine service, marking the successful administration and documentation of the vaccination.

The process begins with the buyer initiating the sequence. The first step involves the buyer logging in as a tenant. Once the login information is submitted, it is sent to the online group purchasing system for verification.

The system then verifies the login details. If the login is invalid, the system displays an error message and prompts the buyer to attempt logging in again. If the login is valid, the system displays the main page to the buyer.

After successfully logging in and viewing the main page, the buyer can choose to view the category list. At this point, the buyer faces a decision: they can either search for a product or enter a feedback message.

If the buyer decides to search for a product, they proceed with the search, and the process concludes for this path.
