If the material is eligible, it is entered into the ANR database, and the purchasing agent purchases the material. If not eligible, the process returns to the research material step.

Once the material is purchased, the distribution agent delivers it to the hospital, completing the process with the requested material delivered.

The process begins when a sales representative at HighTech Store receives a warranty claim. The sales representative then checks the database to verify if the device is under warranty. 

At this point, there are two possible outcomes. If the device is not under warranty, the sales representative will reject the warranty claim, and the process ends with the claim being rejected. If the device is under warranty, the sales representative sends the device to the store technician.

Once the store technician receives the device, they check it to determine the appropriate repair method. There are two possible scenarios here. If the device can be repaired immediately, the store technician repairs the device and then notifies the customer. The process ends with the device being repaired. If the device cannot be repaired right away, the store technician sends it to the workshop technician.

The workshop technician receives the device and researches a solution. After finding a solution, the workshop technician repairs the device and sends it back to the store technician.

Upon receiving the device again, the store technician checks it for any remaining issues. If the issue is resolved, the store technician sends the device back to the sales representative. The sales representative then receives the device and notifies the customer, concluding the process with the device repaired. If the issue is not resolved, the store technician sends the device back to the workshop technician for further repair.

This process ensures that all warranty claims are handled efficiently, with clear steps for both warranty verification and device repair.

The process begins with the logistic manager at Hardware Co. initiating the procedure. The first task for the logistic manager is to acquire the requisition to deliver commodities. Once this is done, the process splits into two parallel tasks.

In one branch, the logistic manager determines whether the request is for a standard or express delivery. This leads to a decision point where the logistic manager must choose between two paths. If the request is identified as a standard delivery, the logistic manager demands more details for verification and then populates the request form. If the request is identified as an express type, the logistic manager demands prices from conveyance providers and then allots the conveyance.

Simultaneously, in the other branch, a warehouse worker bundles the commodities. Both branches eventually converge, and the warehouse worker files the necessary documents and sends the bundled commodities for picking.

The process concludes with the warehouse worker completing the task, marking the end of the procedure.

The process begins with a customer planning a Super Bowl viewing party. The customer starts by researching the best audio and video options using Google. After gathering the necessary information, the customer places an order on the company's website to rent the required equipment.

Once the order is placed, the Audio/Video Company receives the order request. The company then reviews the venue, delivery, and payment information to ensure everything is correct. If any information is incorrect, the company sends a rejection email to the customer, notifying them of the issue.

If all the information is correct, the company checks if all the necessary equipment is available. If any equipment is unavailable, the company again sends a rejection email to the customer. If all equipment is available, the company reserves the equipment and sends the specifications to the delivery and setup department.

The delivery and setup department receives the specifications and coordinates with the venue. The equipment is then delivered to the venue, where the venue staff sets up the equipment. Once the setup is complete, the process concludes with the installation being marked as complete.

The process begins with an engineer initiating the task of creating work instructions. Once the work instructions are prepared, the engineer proceeds to disassemble the system. After disassembly, the process reaches a point where two tasks are carried out simultaneously. The engineer refurbishes materials and, at the same time, cleans and paints the covers. 

Following these parallel tasks, the engineer prepares for assembly by checking the materials. This leads to another point where multiple tasks are executed concurrently. The engineer connects the hardware, puts up the wiring, and prepares the lifting gear all at the same time. 

After these tasks, the engineer updates the software. Concurrently, the engineer mounts the arc, R-tube, and detector, and also orders and installs the FCO. Once these tasks are completed, the engineer mounts the covering. 

The process continues with the engineer moving the system to the bay. Finally, the engineer calibrates the system, marking the end of the process.

The process begins when a decision is made to buy a ticket. This decision is initiated by the ticket vending machine system. The system then requests the required trip information from the commuter. Once the commuter provides the necessary details, the system calculates the payment due for the trip.

After calculating the payment, the system asks the commuter for their preferred payment option. At this point, there is a decision to be made between two payment methods: cash or card.

If the commuter chooses the cash payment option, the ticket vending machine system receives the cash payment. Following this, the system prints the ticket and presents a receipt to the commuter. The commuter then receives the ticket and any change due.

If the commuter opts for the card payment option, the bank authorizes the card payment. Once the payment is authorized, the process continues with the ticket vending machine system printing the ticket and presenting a receipt to the commuter. The commuter receives the ticket, and the process continues as if cash payment was chosen.

After the commuter receives the ticket and any change, the ticket vending machine system informs the commuter that the process is complete. Finally, the process concludes with the system marking the process as completed.

The process begins when the patient arrives at the Accident & Emergency (A&E) department. The patient then walks into the A&E, marking the start of their journey through the hospital's procedures.

Upon entering, the patient is registered by a nurse. After registration, the patient waits to see a nurse for an initial diagnosis. The nurse attends to the patient and provides this initial diagnosis.

Following the nurse's assessment, the patient waits to see a doctor for an official diagnosis. The doctor then provides the official diagnosis.

At this point, the doctor determines whether the patient needs to be admitted to a ward. If the patient needs to be warded, the doctor requests a ward for the patient. The patient then stays in the hospital until a defined date, after which they are discharged upon the doctor's approval.

If the patient does not need to be warded, the doctor assesses whether the patient requires medication. If medication is needed, the doctor prescribes it, and a nurse dispenses the medication to the patient. After receiving the medication, the patient leaves the hospital.

If the patient does not require medication, they leave the hospital immediately after the doctor's assessment. This concludes the patient's journey through the A&E process.

The process begins with the user initiating the workflow. The first task for the user is to validate themselves in the ERP System. Once this is done, the process reaches a decision point. Here, the system checks if the user is valid. If the user is not valid, the RPA BOT rejects the user, and the process ends. If the user is valid, the RPA BOT confirms the credentials and generates a request pop-up.

After the request pop-up is generated, the user enters or hands over tasks in the queue, such as providing an invoice number. The RPA BOT then collects data from CRM systems based on the information provided by the user. Following this, the user validates the generated results. Once validated, the RPA BOT downloads invoices from the server.

The user then analyzes any problems or issues that may have arisen. If problems are identified, the user takes over to address them. Once the user has marked the problems, the RPA BOT resolves any queries, issues, or requests.

After resolving the issues, the process reaches another decision point. If the issues are resolved satisfactorily, the process ends. If not, the RPA BOT generates another request pop-up, and the process loops back to the user entering or handing over tasks in the queue. This cycle continues until all issues are resolved, leading to the end of the process.

The process begins when a customer realizes they have run out of Keurig Coffee Pods. This triggers the start of the process at Amazon. The customer goes online and navigates to the Keurig web page on Amazon's website.

Once the customer is on the Keurig page, Amazon receives the request for the coffee pods. Amazon then obtains the Keurig pods and processes the shipment.

At this point, there is a decision to be made based on whether the customer has an Amazon Prime membership. If the customer does not have Prime, the process ends here. If the customer has Prime, the process continues to the next step.

Simultaneously, the customer is given the opportunity to pay for faster shipping. This leads to another decision point. If the customer accepts the offer for faster shipping, the Keurig k-pods are received in 2 business days. If the customer denies the offer, the Keurig k-pods are received in 4 to 7 business days.

Throughout this process, Amazon manages the tasks and decisions to ensure the customer receives their Keurig Coffee Pods in a timely manner, based on their choices and membership status.

The process begins with the customer initiating a search for locker providers. Once the customer identifies potential providers, they contact our company to express interest.

Our company then takes the lead in identifying the client's needs and submits offers for consideration. The customer reviews the available solutions and decides if our company offers what they need. If the answer is yes, the customer accepts the offer, leading to the creation and sending of a contract by our company. The customer then signs the contract.

Following the contract signing, our company proceeds with the locker design. Once the design is finalized, the customer accepts it, and a prepayment for the locker is made by the customer.

At this point, two parallel activities occur simultaneously. Our company begins the manufacturing order, while also customizing the software for the locker. After the manufacturing order is completed, a decision is made on whether the locker is standard. If it is not standard, HansaAB AS orders the locker parts. If it is standard, the parts are sourced from the warehouse.

HansaAB AS then assembles the locker and delivers it. After delivery, HansaAB AS installs the locker at the customer's location.

Meanwhile, the software customization is completed, and the customer accepts the customized software. Our company then creates the client software package and installs it.

Finally, the customer conducts acceptance testing of the entire locker system. Once the testing is successful, the process concludes with the locker being ready for use. If at any point the customer decides that our company does not offer what they need, the process ends without further action.

The process begins with the customer filling out a registration form. Once the form is completed, a message is sent to the system to initiate the registration process.

The system then starts the registration process by submitting the customer's information. After submission, the system verifies the customer's submission to ensure all necessary information is complete.

Next, the system checks if the submission is complete. If the submission is complete, the system creates master data for the customer and proceeds to input the customer information into the information systems. If the submission is incomplete, the system performs additional checks.

After the customer information is entered into the information systems, the process checks if the registration has been cancelled. If it has been cancelled, a 24-hour timer is set before the process loops back to input the customer information again. If it has not been cancelled, the system sends a SIM card to the customer.

Once the SIM card is sent, the process checks the customer's response. If the customer withdraws from the contract, the process ends. If the customer activates the SIM, they are billed, and a new customer is added to the company, marking the end of the process. If the customer does not reply within two weeks, the SIM card is automatically activated, and the customer is billed, leading to the addition of a new customer and the conclusion of the process.

The process begins with the preparation phase for a roasted chicken. The first step involves gathering all necessary ingredients. Once the ingredients are collected, a list of these ingredients is generated.

Next, the process splits into two tasks that occur simultaneously. One task involves heating the oven to 220 degrees Celsius. At the same time, the chicken is seasoned. After both tasks are completed, the chicken is placed in the oven.

The chicken is then cooked for 5 to 8 minutes. Following this, Jane Doe is added to the process, although the specific role or action is not detailed. The chicken is then allowed to sizzle for 2 minutes.

Subsequently, dates, herbs, and 250 milliliters of water are added to the chicken. The chicken is then roasted for an additional 25 minutes. After this roasting period, 2 tablespoons of Jane Doe are added, again without specific details on the action.

The chicken is cooked for another 20 to 30 minutes. Once this cooking time is completed, the chicken is left to sit for 10 minutes to rest.

Finally, the chicken is carved, and the process concludes with the chicken being served.

The process begins with the borrower initiating the repayment process. The borrower starts by entering the amount they wish to repay. After entering the repayment amount, the borrower selects their preferred payment method. Once the payment method is chosen, the borrower proceeds to select the pay button to continue with the transaction.

Following this, the system redirects the borrower to the payment window. In this window, the borrower makes the payment. After the payment is made, the system takes over to validate the payment.

The system then checks if the payment was successful. If the payment is successful, the system recalculates the borrower's outstanding balance. This recalculation triggers two simultaneous actions: updating the outstanding balance and updating the debt repayment amount. Once both updates are completed, the system sends a success message to the borrower.

If the payment is not successful, the system sends an error message to the borrower, indicating that the payment did not go through.

The process concludes with the system ending the transaction, regardless of whether the payment was successful or not.

The process begins when the Pasta & Risotto expert receives an order for pasta sauce. This initiates the preparation process in the Italian kitchen.

First, the Pasta & Risotto expert starts by heating oil. Simultaneously, the Nephews & Nieces begin their tasks. They start by chopping onions, followed by chopping ham. Once these tasks are completed, both the chopped onions and ham are ready for the next step.

At this point, the process splits into two parallel paths. On one path, the Nephews & Nieces continue by chopping tomatoes and then proceed to chop chili peppers. On the other path, the Pasta & Risotto expert takes the heated oil and uses it to fry the chopped onions and ham together.

After frying the onions and ham, the Pasta & Risotto expert adds wine to the mixture. Following this, they season the mixture with salt to enhance the flavor.

Once the tomatoes and chili peppers are chopped, they are added to the mixture by the Pasta & Risotto expert. This combines all the ingredients together.

The final step in the cooking process is to cook the sauce until it is ready. Once the sauce is fully cooked, the Pasta & Risotto expert hands it over to Nonnina, marking the end of the process.

The process begins when a client sends an order to the Medi-Check Group at Lane Cove HCC Pharmacy. Upon receiving the order, the Medi-Check Group initiates the process by acknowledging the order.

The first task is for the Medi-Check Group to receive the order. Once the order is received, the next step involves selecting a pharmacist based on the client's specific requests, such as language or gender preferences. This selection is handled by the Medi-Check Group.

After selecting the appropriate pharmacist, the Medi-Check Group schedules a time for the service. Following the scheduling, the process reaches a point where two tasks are carried out simultaneously. The first task involves preparing the order, which includes gathering necessary equipment and any common medicines required. The second task is scheduling an Uber for transportation.

Once both tasks are completed, the Medi-Check Group proceeds to visit the client's home. During this visit, the service is provided to the client. After completing the service, the Medi-Check Group returns to the pharmacy.

Upon returning, the accounting department at Lane Cove HCC Pharmacy prepares an invoice. This invoice includes the amount due and the payment due date. The invoice is then issued to the client.

The process then enters a waiting phase for the payment. If the payment is not received, the process loops back to reissue the invoice. If the payment is received, the accounting department sends a payment receipt to the client.

Finally, the process concludes with the end of the transaction, marking the completion of the service and payment cycle.

The process begins with the Cheese and Wine Buyer at Z Chedd'r initiating the task of reviewing inventory records. Following this, the buyer contacts various stores to gather their inventory counts. After collecting this information, the buyer checks the physical inventory in the warehouse to ensure accuracy.

Next, the buyer considers sales trends and seasonal demand to assess the need for wine and cheese products. Based on this analysis, the buyer determines the necessity for ordering additional products. If needed, the buyer proceeds to call suppliers to place an order for the required items.

Once the order is placed, the buyer determines the timing for the shipment. At this point, a decision is made regarding the shipment's timing: if the shipment is late, the buyer arranges for a van to pick up the order. If the shipment is on time, it is received by the Shipping and Receiving Clerk.

After the shipment is received, the buyer authorizes payment for the order. The buyer then sends the supplier's invoice to the accountant for further processing. The accountant receives and reviews the supplier's invoice and determines the payment amounts for each supplier.

The accountant then decides whether there are multiple payments to be made or just one. If there are multiple payments, they are combined into a single payment amount. Finally, the accountant pays the supplier, concluding the process.

The process begins when the user opens the app. The user then selects the type of log they wish to access. At this point, the process checks if it is the user's first login. If it is not the first login, the user is prompted to choose whether they are a caregiver or a nurse. If the user is a caregiver, they proceed to enter their data, followed by entering the babies' data. After entering the babies' data, the caregiver opens the booking list to check the baby's status. If the baby's status is good, the caregiver opens the menu of scion, selects the scion and time, and confirms the booking. If the baby's status is not good, the process ends with the caregiver waiting for the situation to improve.

If the user is a nurse, they enter the data of the health center and determine the amount of scion needed. They then set the appointment time. If the baby has taken the scion, the nurse puts a check behind the baby's name, and the process ends with the baby having taken the scion. If the baby has not taken the scion, the nurse adds the baby to the lagging behind list and sends a notification to booking.

If it is the user's first login, they must register before proceeding further in the process.

The business process begins with the Planning Director receiving an order. The Planning Director then processes the list of manufacturing orders. During this task, the information is stored in the BAAN system. After processing, the Planning Director validates the list of manufacturing orders. Once validated, the Planning Director prints the manufacturing orders, again utilizing the BAAN system for data storage. The printed orders are then delivered by the Planning Director, marking the end of the planning phase.

Next, the Warehouse Manager receives the manufacturing orders. These orders are initially stored as a data object. The Warehouse Manager then distributes the manufacturing orders to the Upholstery Section. This marks the transition from planning to production.

In the production phase, the Upholstery Section receives the manufacturing orders. A parallel gateway is then activated, allowing two tasks to occur simultaneously. The first task involves the Upholstery Section cutting the Jane Doe to the chair. The second task involves the Warehouse Manager collecting the needed materials. Once the materials are collected, the Upholstery Section glues the foam.

After the foam is glued, the Upholstery Section covers the foam with fabric. Following this, every chair component is assembled by the Upholstery Section. Once assembled, the Upholstery Section packs the chair.

The packed chair is then received by the Warehouse Manager as a completed product. The Warehouse Manager updates the manufacturing orders' state and sends the products, marking the completion of the manufacturing orders. Finally, the process concludes with the Warehouse Manager acknowledging that the manufacturing orders are completed.

The process begins when a customer arrives at the First Country Hotel. The customer starts by entering their reservation details into the system.

Once the reservation details are entered, the kiosk at the hotel takes over to verify the reservation. The kiosk checks if the reservation is found in the system. If the reservation is not found, the kiosk displays a message indicating that no reservation was found, and the process ends with a prompt to contact customer service.

If the reservation is found, the kiosk proceeds to allocate an available room for the customer. After allocating the room, the kiosk displays the reservation details for the customer to review.

The customer then confirms the displayed details. Following this confirmation, the customer makes the necessary payment for their stay.

After the payment is completed, the process splits into two simultaneous tasks. The kiosk provides the customer with a room key and an electronic receipt. Once both the room key and e-receipt are provided, the customer takes them.

Finally, the process concludes with the customer successfully checking in to the hotel.

The process begins with the Customer Service Team at PickPark receiving information from a customer. Once they have this information, they proceed to send an appointment for maintenance to the customer. The customer then receives this appointment and decides whether to approve or not.

If the customer does not approve the appointment, they request a change in the time and date. This request is sent back to the Customer Service Team, who will then send a new appointment for maintenance.

If the customer approves the appointment, they send the problem details to the Customer Service Team. Along with this, they also provide additional information about the extent of damage to CCTV and sensors.

Upon receiving the problem details, the Customer Service Team prepares these details and sends them to the Maintenance Team. The Maintenance Team then receives the problem details and prepares the team and equipment needed for the maintenance task.

Once the team and equipment are ready, the Maintenance Team proceeds to the site to perform maintenance. After completing the maintenance, they reach a decision point. If the maintenance is finished without any issues, the process ends. However, if there are problems during maintenance, the Maintenance Team receives further problem details from the Customer Service Team and the process loops back to preparing the team and equipment again.

The process begins when a customer needs legal advice. The customer starts by logging into Lexoo. Once logged in, the customer fills out a form detailing their legal needs.

After the form is completed, it is reviewed by customer service. At this point, customer service checks if additional information is required. If more information is needed, the customer is asked to provide it. Once the additional information is provided, the form is reviewed again by customer service.

If no additional information is needed, customer service creates a Request for Proposal (RFP). This RFP is then sent to a lawyer, who responds to it. After the lawyer responds, customer service collects quotes from various lawyers.

The customer then reviews these quotes and selects a lawyer. Once a lawyer is chosen, customer service notifies the selected lawyer. The process concludes with the notification, marking the completion of the process.

The process begins with the Risk Management Team initiating the procedure. They start by checking the instrument rating. Once this task is completed, they proceed to check the imposed rating. At this point, a decision is made based on whether the rating is known or unknown. If the rating is unknown, the team checks the fall-safe rating. If the rating is known, they determine the imposed rating.

After determining the imposed rating, the team moves on to determine the instrument rating. This leads to another task where they determine the instrument rating category. Following this, a decision is made based on whether the rating has changed or remained unchanged. If the rating has changed, the Risk Management Team updates the liquidity flow and informs the Collateral Management Team. If the rating remains unchanged, the process ends for the Risk Management Team.

Simultaneously, if the fall-safe rating is known, the team determines the fall-safe rating. If it is unknown, they find that there is no rating. Both these paths lead to determining the instrument rating, which then connects back to determining the instrument rating category.

Once the Collateral Management Team is informed about the updated liquidity flow, they adjust the rating accordingly. This marks the end of the process for the Collateral Management Team.

The process begins when an employee identifies a need for training. The employee starts by creating a leave application. Once the application is prepared, the employee sends the request to the section managers.

The section managers receive the leave application request and proceed to check the duration of the leave. At this point, they determine if the leave is over two weeks. If the leave is not over two weeks, the section managers approve the leave, and the process is completed.

If the leave is over two weeks, the section managers send the request to the division manager. The division manager receives the leave request and checks the associated expenses. The division manager then evaluates if the expenses are above $7,000. If the expenses are not above $7,000, the division manager approves the request, and the process is completed.

If the expenses exceed $7,000, the division manager sends the leave request to the vice president. The vice president receives the leave application and checks the return on investment (ROI). The vice president then decides if the ROI is good. If the ROI is deemed good, the vice president approves the request, and the process is completed.

If the ROI is not satisfactory, the vice president rejects the application, and the process is completed.

The process begins with the customer initiating an order. The customer first determines the payment method they wish to use. There are two options available: "Cash On Delivery" or "Prepayment."

If the customer chooses "Cash On Delivery," they proceed to request product information. After receiving the product information from the staff, the customer checks the availability of the requested products. If the products are not available, the customer cancels the order, and the process ends with the order being marked as cancelled. If the products are available, the customer determines the quantity of the requested products and records this information into the sales order system.

If the customer opts for "Prepayment," they request a quotation. At this point, the availability of a manager is checked. If the manager is not available, the customer cancels the order, and the process ends with the order being marked as cancelled. If the manager is available, the customer receives the quotation from the manager and then determines the products, quantity, and delivery date. This information is then recorded by the manager, who also declares the payment terms and conditions. The process concludes with the order being fulfilled.

Once the products and quantities are recorded into the sales order system, the staff generates a customer sales order invoice. Following this, the staff receives payment from the customer. The process concludes with the order being fulfilled.

The process begins with ABC company starting the procedure. The first task is for ABC company to publish a job advertisement. Once the job advertisement is published, a candidate detects the vacancy. After detecting the vacancy, the candidate proceeds to acquire the vacancy.

At this point, the process splits into two parallel tasks. The candidate simultaneously sends a request to acquire the vacancy and provides a receipt for payment. Both tasks are completed at the same time, and the candidate then waits for a response.

Once the candidate is expecting a response, the interviewer receives the request for the required vacancy. The interviewer reviews the requisition again and then conducts an interview with the candidate.

After the interview, a decision is made. If the candidate is chosen, the interviewer selects the applicant and notifies them about getting the vacancy. The candidate then fills up a selection form, marking the end of the process.

If the candidate is not chosen, the interviewer declines the applicant and notifies them of the decision. This also leads to the end of the process.

The process begins with Jane Doe monitoring the virus. She then gathers information about the first case. After obtaining this information, Jane Doe proceeds to monitor the cases.

At this point, Jane Doe evaluates whether the cases are rapidly increasing. If they are, she increases testing and advises social distancing and self-quarantine. Following this, she checks if people are still going out. If they are, she allows restaurants and bars to operate only for takeout and delivery to stop the spread. She then assesses whether the cases have reached a steady number. If not, she closes all non-essential places such as schools and salons, and forces non-essential workers to work from home. She also advises people to use public transportation only if necessary and continues to monitor their activities. This leads to making more decisions if needed.

If the cases are not rapidly increasing, Jane Doe continues to monitor the cases. This leads to the end of the process.

If people are not going out, Jane Doe continues to monitor the situation, which leads to the end of the process.

If the cases are at a steady number, Jane Doe continues monitoring for changes but determines that no further restrictions are needed, leading to the end of the process.

The business process begins with the HR Department at Enatex Metals Sdn Bhd initiating the process. They start by broadcasting training courses to employees. Once the announcement is made, employees receive the information about the available courses.

Employees then decide if they are interested in the training. If an employee is not interested, the process ends for them. However, if they are interested, they request a training application form from the HR Department.

Upon receiving the request, the HR Department sends the training application form to the interested employee. The employee then fills out the application form and submits it back to the HR Department.

After submission, the HR Department waits for a response from the manager. If the waiting time exceeds three days, the manager sends a reminder message. If not, the manager proceeds to check the employee's qualifications.

The manager then decides whether to approve the application. If the application is not approved, the manager rejects the application form and sends a rejection message to the employee, ending the process for that application. If the application is approved, the manager approves the training application and sends an approval message to the employee, concluding the process successfully.

The process begins when the HCC Administrative Systems receive a patient booking. The system then records the patient booking details. Following this, the system checks whether the patient is new or existing.

If the patient is new, the system checks the registration form and MyHealth record access. If the registration form is not complete, the system informs the patient to complete the form. Once the form is completed, the process ends.

If the patient is existing or the new patient's registration form is complete, the booking is accepted. The system then sends a confirmation to the patient.

Next, the patient has a consultation with the HCC Pharmacy. During this consultation, a general checkup is conducted. Following the checkup, the patient's medicine management is reviewed. The pharmacist then discusses any necessary medicine change plans with the patient.

After discussing the medicine change plan, the patient is referred to Live Well Home Care Services. An appointment is booked with Live Well, and there is a waiting period of one week.

Once the booking is confirmed by Live Well, a confirmation is sent to the patient. Live Well then explains the plan as per the package to the patient and obtains confirmation from the patient.

If the patient accepts the service, Live Well prepares a personalized plan on nutrition and exercise. This plan is then carried out as discussed. If the patient does not accept the service, the process ends.

The process begins with the Office of the Vice President initiating a task to start the process. Following this, the Office of the Vice President notifies the student about the situation. This notification is also communicated to the student through a message.

Next, the process reaches a decision point where the Office of the Vice President determines whether an agreement has been reached. If an agreement is reached, the process concludes with the Office of the Vice President determining the consequences. If no agreement is reached, the Office of the Vice President schedules a meeting.

Once the meeting is scheduled, a facilitator becomes involved to assist in the process. The facilitator's involvement leads to a meeting conducted by the Academic Honesty Panel. During this meeting, the Academic Honesty Panel determines a resolution.

After the resolution is determined, the Academic Honesty Panel sends a written notice, which is also communicated to the student. The facilitator then sends a written notice to both parties involved.

The process then reaches another decision point where the Academic Honesty Panel checks if both parties show up. If both parties do not show up, the panel determines if a violation occurred and establishes the consequences. If both parties do show up, the panel meets in private to discuss further.

Following the private meeting, the Academic Honesty Panel assesses whether the instructor has met their responsibilities. If the instructor has met their responsibilities, the panel imposes the consequence. If not, nothing is imposed.

Throughout the process, the instructor is involved through a separate communication channel, receiving messages from the Office of the Vice President. The student is also involved through a separate communication channel, receiving messages from both the Office of the Vice President and the Academic Honesty Panel.

The process begins with a front office employee at Hand-made Cosmetics (HMC) receiving an order. Once the order is received, the same employee prepares the product specification. After preparing the specification, the employee checks if there are enough materials in the inventory. If the materials are sufficient, the employee sends the product specification.

At this point, the process splits into two parallel paths. In the first path, a manufacturing department technician receives the product specification and prepares the basis of the product. After preparing the basis, the technician updates the inventory and tests the basis of the product. There is a 30-minute waiting period before the technician checks if the test results are satisfactory. If the results are not satisfactory, the technician re-does the basis of the product and updates the inventory again. If the results are satisfactory, the process continues to the next step.

In the second parallel path, a manufacturing department specialist receives the product specification and prepares the active substance. After preparing the active substance, the specialist updates the inventory. The specialist then prepares a sample final product and tests the sample. If the test succeeds, the specialist prepares the product for the customer. If the test does not succeed, the specialist re-does the active substance and updates the inventory again.

Once both parallel paths are completed successfully, the front office employee prepares the package, marking the end of the process.

The process begins when there is a need for a BTG session. The first step involves checking the availability of an Emergency Medical Officer (EMO). If the EMO is unavailable, the next possible EMO is called. If the EMO is available, they are contacted directly.

Once an EMO is contacted, emergency staff is assigned to the case. The BTG session is then started, and the emergency staff logs in. After logging in, the staff views the Electronic Health Record (EHR) of the patient. The next step involves examining the patient and reviewing the information gathered.

At this point, a decision is made based on the details gathered. If no further details are gathered, the process moves to deciding on further treatment. If further details are gathered, additional information is obtained before deciding on treatment.

Once a decision on treatment is made, several actions occur simultaneously. The patient may be directed to surgery, further consultation, or immunization/investigations. Additionally, a prescription for a simple condition may be provided.

If the patient is directed to surgery or immunization/investigations, a prescription for a complex condition is given, followed by admitting the patient to the ward. After admission, the emergency staff logs out, and the BTG session ends. This marks the end of the BTG condition process.

The process begins when the manager initiates the requirements analysis process. The first task is for the development team to conduct a domain analysis. Once this is completed, the manager defines the scope of the project.

Following the scope definition, the process splits into two parallel tasks. The manager simultaneously defines the functional requirements and the non-functional requirements. After both sets of requirements are defined, the manager prioritizes them.

Next, the development team estimates the required time for the tasks. Once the time estimation is complete, the manager enters the requirements into the JIRA backlog.

The manager then reviews the requirements. At this point, a decision is made. If the requirements need updating, the manager updates them and assigns tasks to developers. If no updates are necessary, the manager directly assigns tasks to developers.

Finally, the process concludes with the end of the requirement analysis process.

The process begins when a new business application is initiated by the business. The first step involves the business initiating a business request. Once the request is initiated, it is sent to the system administrator, who receives the request.

The system administrator then submits the resource request to the integration team. The integration team is responsible for validating the business request. At this point, a decision is made. If the request is not valid, the integration team rejects the request and informs the system administrator of the rejection reasons. The system administrator then notifies the business of the rejection reasons, and the business receives a rejection notice. The business can then update the business request and resubmit it.

If the request is valid, the integration team proceeds to allocate system resources. After the resources are allocated, the system administrator builds the servers with the operating system and business application.

Once the servers are built, the business performs a quality check on the business application. If the quality check is successful, the business makes the application live for business use. The process concludes with the business application resource being ready for use.

The process begins with the task of accessing the student profile on Swim Central. This task is performed by the person responsible for applying accreditation. Once the student profile is accessed, the next step is to select the accreditations available for the student.

After selecting the accreditations, the process continues with choosing what is available. This is followed by typing the accreditation type into the search field to find the specific accreditation needed.

Once the accreditation type is identified, the next step is to select it. At this point, a decision must be made regarding the type of accreditation process to follow. There are three possible paths:

1. If the path chosen is for Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), the next task is to upload the RPL certificate to the Teacher ID.
2. If the path is for a new course (New CS), the task is to upload the Statement of Attainment (SOA).
3. If the path is for reaccreditation, the task is to upload the reaccreditation certificate into the Teacher ID.

After completing any of these tasks, the process converges to a point where the certificate is uploaded into the Teacher ID.

Following this, another decision point is reached. Here, the process diverges based on the type of applicant:

1. If the applicant is Australian, the next task is to upload the Working with Children Check (WWCC). After this, the process concludes with the action of pressing apply.
2. If the applicant is international, the process directly concludes with the action of pressing apply.

This structured approach ensures that all necessary documents are uploaded and the correct accreditation path is followed based on the applicant's status and the type of accreditation being applied for.

The process begins with ACME Warehouse initiating the resupply cycle. The first task is to check the inventory level. If the inventory is at or below the minimum level, a purchase order is created. If the inventory is above the minimum level, the process ends.

Once a purchase order is created, it is reviewed. During the review, the purchase order can either be approved or rejected. If approved, the next step is to reserve funds for the purchase. If rejected, the purchase order is reworked and reviewed again.

After funds are reserved, the purchase order is sent to the supplier. This action triggers two simultaneous tasks: receiving the packaging slip and receiving the invoice. Once both tasks are completed, the information is recorded.

Following the recording of information, the reserved funds are released. Subsequently, payment is issued to the supplier. This marks the end of the process.

The process begins when a user visits the homepage. At this point, the user is presented with three options: continue as a guest, register as a new user, or log in. Each of these choices leads the user to search for their desired item.

Once the user searches for an item, they proceed to select the item based on size. After selecting the item, the user encounters a decision point regarding the number of items they have chosen. If the user selects multiple items, they can either add the items to their wishlist or add them to their cart. If the user chooses to add items to their wishlist, the process ends there. If they add items to their cart, they then proceed to view their cart.

If the user selects only one item, they have the option to click "Buy Now," which leads them to change or add their address. After updating the address, the user selects their preferred payment mode and makes the payment. Once the payment is processed, the process concludes.

For users who added items to their cart, after viewing the cart, they proceed to place the order. This step completes the process for users who have added items to their cart.

The process begins with the manufacturing team starting the loading of produce. Once the produce is ready, the manufacturing team loads it into a container. During this task, a forklift is used to assist with the loading process.

After the container is loaded, the manufacturing team sets the conditions inside the container to ensure the goods are preserved properly. Following this, the container is loaded onto a truck by the manufacturing team.

Next, the container is transferred from the truck to a ship, with the assistance of a crane. Once the container is on the ship, the manufacturing team plugs in the container's power supply to maintain the necessary conditions during transit.

At this point, there is a decision to be made. The manufacturing team can either monitor the container's condition or proceed with the ship setting sail. If the container's condition is monitored, the process continues until the ship is ready to depart. Once the ship sets sail, it travels to its destination.

Upon arrival at the destination, the manufacturing team unplugs the container's power supply. The container is then unloaded from the ship to a truck, again using a crane for assistance.

The container is then delivered to a distributor. Upon delivery, the distributor unloads the goods from the container and performs quality control checks to ensure everything is in order. After passing quality control, the goods are transferred to a warehouse using a forklift.

In the warehouse, the distributor monitors the warehouse conditions to ensure the goods remain in good condition. The inventory is then updated to reflect the new stock levels.

Following inventory updates, the distributor picks and packs the goods for shipment to the retailer. During this stage, the shipment condition is monitored to ensure everything is maintained properly.

Finally, the goods are shipped to the retailer. Upon arrival, the retailer receives the shipment, marking the end of the process.

The process begins with the patient initiating the procedure. Immediately, two parallel activities occur. The front desk receives the patient, and the system logs into the website.

At the front desk, the staff checks if the patient has an appointment. If the patient has an appointment, the front desk checks the patient's health record. If not, the system proceeds to book an appointment for the patient.

Simultaneously, the system books an appointment and processes the payment. After the payment is made, the system generates both an appointment ticket and a payment receipt. The appointment ticket is then used to proceed with the patient's visit.

Once the appointment ticket is generated, the doctor receives the patient and conducts an examination. Following the examination, the system updates the patient's medical record.

Finally, the process concludes with the patient receiving the payment receipt, marking the end of the procedure.

The process begins when an intern receives a customer referral. The intern then inputs the customer data into the system. This data is stored in the CKUGA database.

Next, the intern checks if bag tags are available. If no bag tags are available, the intern prints a new bag tag. If bag tags are available, the intern reuses an existing tag. After handling the bag tags, the intern prints meal planning and bag list reports.

The intern then sends these reports and the meal menu to the kitchen. The kitchen staff plans the meals and then splits into two groups. Two-thirds of the kitchen staff prepare the food, while the remaining one-third fill the bags.

Meanwhile, the drivers get delivery instructions. After receiving the instructions, they pick up the bags and then the precooked meal containers. The drivers deliver the food and note the number of containers returned. They also note if the food was delivered and any additional notes.

After completing the deliveries, the drivers drop off the bags, containers, and coolers. They then turn in the filled-out forms. The intern enters this information into the system, which is also stored in the CKUGA database. Finally, the process is complete.
